lead_headline: Astro's background dev server takes shape; AI SDK opens subagent prototype
lead_body: The bulk of Monday's activity settled in Astro and the AI SDK. Astro's commit run built out experimental background dev-server scaffolding — lock files, SIGKILL fallback, log tailing — while the AI SDK opened a subagent prototype and landed AbortSignal support for long-running Google agent streams. Metaflow closed the night with 2.19.29.
lead_article:
The day's heaviest traffic split across Astro and the AI SDK, with Metaflow closing the night on a point release. Astro's commit run was dominated by background dev-server management — experimental scaffolding for running the dev server as a detached background process, complete with a lock file layer migrated from the JS API down to the CLI, a SIGKILL fallback after SIGTERM timeout, and a new --follow flag for tailing logs. Alongside that, a fix for infinite spawn recursion when agent environment variables are inherited suggests the background-server machinery was already hitting edge cases in testing. A separate PR opened late afternoon targets dev-mode styles missing from content-collection entries, and SSR routes broken by dynamic prerendered routes got patched in the same window. Astro also cut a changeset to major, which is worth noting.

The AI SDK pushed a subagent prototype to an open PR — notable given the broader direction — while landed commits added flexible tool descriptions, instructions as prepareStep input, and AbortSignal support for cancelling long-running Google Interactions API agents mid-stream. A fix for accumulative properties on StreamTextResult and GenerateTextResult cleaned up some accounting debt. Metaflow shipped 2.19.29 with a follow-on PYTHONPATH fix merged just before midnight and a new PR opening Bokeh integration. Workflow SDK rolled workflow@5.0.0-beta.5. Claude Code released v2.1.139 quietly; the bug queue is louder than the release, with a schema-hallucination report and a Korean output regression on Opus 4.7 both sitting open.
